core_obligations: Construct the top horizontal short exact sequence: from K_n as a shift of the cone on f^n : K -> K obtain the inverse system 0 -> H^p(K)/f^n H^p(K) -> H^p(K_n) -> H^{p+1}(K)[f^n] -> 0, and take inverse limits using the Mittag-Leffler lemma (proof lines 26960-26968).

To prove commutativity, introduce L = tau_{<= p}K -> K and set L_n = L tensor^L_A (A --f^n--> A), obtaining a map (L_n) -> (K_n) of inverse systems and the displayed map of short exact sequences (proof lines 26971-26987).
Compute the entries using H^i(L) = 0 for i > p and H^p(L) = H^p(K): show H^p(L-hat) = H^0(H^p(K)-hat) and H^p(L_n) = H^p(K)/f^n H^p(K) (proof lines 26988-26991).

Note H^{p-1}(L_n) = H^{p-1}(K_n), and conclude the isomorphism displayed in the statement using that the kernel of H^0(H^p(K)-hat) -> the f-adic completion of H^p(K) equals R^1 lim H^p(K)[f^n] (proof lines 26992-26996).

Complete the commutativity of the diagram; the author states that the verification that the rightmost square commutes (with the top row defined as in the first paragraph) is omitted (proof lines 26996-26999).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring A, an element f, and an object K of D(A), sets K_n = K tensor^L_A (A --f^n--> A), and asserts that for every p there is a commutative diagram with exact rows and columns whose entries are the f-adic completion of H^p(K), the limit of the H^p(K_n), the functor T_f of H^{p+1}(K), H^0 of the completion of H^p(K), the cohomology H^p(K-hat) of the derived completion, and the two R^1 limit terms, with the left vertical and middle horizontal short exact sequences taken from a specified example and the middle vertical one from a specified lemma (source lines 26927-26957). The proof is a real construction, not a citation. It first builds the top horizontal short exact sequence from the inverse system of short exact sequences 0 -> H^p(K)/f^n H^p(K) -> H^p(K_n) -> H^{p+1}(K)[f^n] -> 0, which come from the description of K_n as a shift of the cone on f^n, by taking inverse limits and using the Mittag-Leffler lemma (proof lines 26960-26968). It then proves commutativity by introducing L = tau_{<= p}K and comparing the inverse systems (L_n) and (K_n) through the displayed map of short exact sequences (proof lines 26971-26987). The substantive computation is that, since H^i(L) = 0 for i > p and H^p(L) = H^p(K), one gets H^p(L-hat) = H^0(H^p(K)-hat) and H^p(L_n) = H^p(K)/f^n H^p(K), while H^{p-1}(L_n) = H^{p-1}(K_n), and the stated isomorphism follows because the kernel of H^0(H^p(K)-hat) -> the f-adic completion of H^p(K) is already known to be R^1 lim H^p(K)[f^n] (proof lines 26988-26996). The author then states that the verification that the rightmost square commutes is omitted (proof lines 26996-26999). The non-routine content is the truncation comparison that computes the entries of the diagram.
